title: Paid social pays back, but retargeting doesn't
subtitle: A 28-market geo holdout shows paid social returns $2.15 per dollar, well under the 5.6× the platforms report. Nearly all of the gap is in retargeting, so we recommend moving $3.4M of it into prospecting and new tests.
summary: A six-week matched-market holdout across 28 DMAs shows paid social drives real revenue: 2.15× incremental ROAS, against the 5.6× the platforms report. Prospecting clears our 1.8× hurdle at 2.81×. Retargeting returns only 0.97×, so we recommend moving $3.4M out of it for an expected +$2.0M a year in revenue.
key_findings: Pausing paid social cut revenue in holdout markets by 4.1% (95% CI 2.7–5.5%): $3.95M of revenue on $1.84M of withheld spend.
Blended incremental ROAS is 2.15× vs. 5.6× platform-reported, so the platforms over-credit by about 2.6×.
Prospecting iROAS is 2.81× (over-credit 1.5×). Retargeting is 0.97× (over-credit 8.1×), below the 1.8× hurdle.
Moving $3.4M from retargeting into prospecting ($2.4M) and a test reserve ($1.0M) should add about $2.0M a year in revenue at flat spend.
